clue.text: Band's journey through the Home Counties

indicators.note: the journey is placed through, i.e. inside, the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties round London, in the South East, abbreviated SE
a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: A rock band tours the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, which is what a band on a flag or shirt is.

clue.text: Party-goer, i.e. A-list company, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation are used without dots
the letters of the word without its hyphen

explanation.surface: A guest at the party asks whether the firm counts as celebrity company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IEALISTCO, from 'i.e.', 'A-list' and CO (company).
explanation.definitionFit: A person who frequents fashionable gatherings is a socially prominent person, a regular at parties.

clue.text: Story's an introduction to Caesar in his city

indicators.note: the letters go inside the name of Caesar's city

parts.note: Caesar's city is Rome

indicators.note: introduction to picks the first letter of Caesar

explanation.surface: A tale introduces Julius Caesar in the city he ruled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his city' is Rome, Caesar's city; AN plus C (the first letter of 'Caesar') goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of love or adventure, or a fanciful invented account, is a kind of narrative.

clue.text: Stop apricots being stewed for snack food

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Don't stew apricots when you want a quick snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being stewed' rearranges the letters of STOP and APRICOTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin fried slices of tuber sold in bags are a popular savoury snack, called chips in the US.

clue.text: Sailors taking on the world appear wholly engaging

indicators.note: the sailors take on, i.e. add, the world after themselves

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS is the plural
an orb is a globe, so the world

explanation.surface: A crew of sailors with the whole world before them look utterly captivating.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross or occupy someone's attention completely is to engage them wholly.

clue.text: Mention item of jewellery found in turning over bar

indicators.note: the jewellery is found inside the reversed bar
turning over says the word for a bar is read backwards

parts.note: a pub is a bar
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone raises the subject of a ring discovered while tidying a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes PUB into BUP, and RING goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or introduce a subject in conversation is to refer to it.

clue.text: Theatrical production in square posters sent up

indicators.note: sent up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stage show is advertised on square posters put up around town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sent up' reverses: AREPO runs across 'squARE POsters' and reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged work set to music, with singers and orchestra, is a form of drama.

clue.text: 60s rebel to get better of upset family

parts.note: to beat is to get the better of

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for family upside down, so backwards

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: A young rebel of the sixties defies his disapproving relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns KIN into NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the bohemian counterculture of the late 1950s and 60s was a nonconformist dropout.

clue.text: One not entirely lifeless concept

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: lifeless means dead

explanation.surface: A notion that is only half dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims DEAD to DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought or notion formed in the mind is a mental conception.

clue.text: Inflict great damage on returning vermin in time

indicators.note: the vermin go inside the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: returning says the vermin word is read backwards

parts.note: mice are vermin

explanation.surface: Rats or mice coming back to a house can wreck it in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MICE into ECIM, which goes inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy a large proportion of something is to wreak great damage on it.

clue.text: Films blokes kept back in custody of spies

indicators.note: the blokes are held inside the spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: kept back says the word for blokes is read backwards

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: A few men are being detained by intelligence agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' turns MEN into NEM, which sits inside CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema is the film industry or films collectively, as in 'French cinema'.

clue.text: Encouraging eating mushy peas? That's mean

indicators.note: the encouraging word eats, i.e. takes inside, the mashed letters

parts.note: cheering means encouraging

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner is egged on to finish his mushy peas, which is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' rearranges PEAS into SEPA, which 'eating' puts inside CHEERING; mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stingy over trivial sums, like a miser paring rind from cheese, is being miserly.

clue.text: Not favouring whisky, unlike everyone else?

explanation.surface: A drinker turns down whisky while all the others happily drink it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means opposed to grain whisky; as an idiom it means contrary to the natural or usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is a kind of whisky, so opposing it is being set against it; the idiom means going contrary to common inclination, as a nonconformist does.

clue.text: Supposed expert showing main source of current in flex

indicators.note: the sea and the letter go inside the word for flex

parts.note: a flex is an electric wire
the main is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An electrician claims expertise in finding where the mains current enters the cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks electrical beside 'current' and 'flex', but it is the sea; 'source of' takes C from 'current'.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who thinks himself clever is a self-styled authority, a would-be sage.

clue.text: Courage and power leading to good fortune

indicators.note: the power letter comes first, leading on to good fortune

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
good fortune is luck

explanation.surface: Bravery and strength bring their own good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck is spirit or nerve, the bravery to face danger.

clue.text: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified

definitions.text: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified

parts.words: One whose field of expertise hasn't been identified
parts.note: reads as a specialist in a vague subject, but means one who studies objects in the sky that are unidentified

explanation.surface: A scholar whose speciality nobody can pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't been identified' points to the U in UFO, an unidentified flying object.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies reports of unidentified flying objects is an expert on things not yet identified.

clue.text: Satisfies hunting groups

explanation.surface: The hunt gives its members what they want.
explanation.definitionFit: To fulfil a need or demand is to answer it; a hunt's gathering of riders and hounds is called by the same word.

clue.text: Spooky horse seen around hansom

indicators.note: the horse is seen placed around the carriage

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a hansom is a horse-drawn cab

explanation.surface: An eerie horse appears beside an old hansom cab in the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome and associated with death is grimly eerie.

clue.text: Left to tuck into hot sweet fruitcake

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside the word for hot

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone is left to eat warm fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' means stolen, as in hot goods; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German Christmas bread rich with dried fruit and marzipan is a sweet fruit loaf.

clue.text: Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather (3-5)' is for a hyphenated 3-5 answer about protection from cold; it does not fit IDEATION, and no search found the matching clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Cope with rain in storm? It should protect against colder weather

clue.text: In that place is a saint

parts.note: in that place means there
is contracted to an apostrophe S

explanation.surface: A holy figure is pointed out over there.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'there's a', the clue gives the name of St Theresa (of Avila or Lisieux).
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa of Avila and Thérèse of Lisieux are canonised holy women of that name.

clue.text: Writing for oneself, not novel as literary work?

parts.note: something not novel is ordinary or everyday
a book is a literary work

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether a private journal, being unoriginal, counts as literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' tempts as the noun beside 'literary work', but here it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: A notebook in which a person copies quotations and thoughts for private use is kept by the writer for personal reference.

clue.text: Mother — and her relationship with father?

explanation.surface: A mother wonders about her bond with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: MATER is Latin, and public-school slang, for mother; read as MATE-R, it is the one who is father's mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for one's female parent; she is also father's partner, his mate, the one he paired with.

clue.text: English county known to Scots

explanation.surface: A Scot is familiar with a county in England.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, to 'ken' is to know, and its past participle is 'kent'. Kent is the county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in south-east England, and in Scots dialect the past tense of ken, meaning familiar or recognised.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar's courage

explanation.surface: A Babylonian king is praised for his daring.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nebuchadnezzar is a giant wine bottle holding twenty standard bottles; 'bottle' is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wine containers are named after biblical kings, and in British slang nerve or daring is called by the same word.

clue.text: One kind of European, or second kind of European

parts.note: an Iberian is someone from Spain or Portugal

explanation.surface: A classification of Europeans offers two types.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the definition: someone from the Russian region east of the Urals. The second half builds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the vast Russian region beyond the Urals is a type of Russian, a citizen of a European country.

clue.text: Queen's tirade not following usual custom?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: The monarch breaks with protocol by delivering an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: something straying from the accepted course.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from the proper course or standard means departing from the expected path.

clue.text: Shocked as snow's beginning in a mountain pass

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for a mountain pass

parts.note: a ghat is a mountain pass in India

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of the word snow

explanation.surface: Travellers are horrified as snow begins to fall in a high pass.
explanation.walkthrough: GHAT is an Indian word for a mountain pass; 'beginning' gives S from 'snow's', placed inside it after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horrified or stunned is being struck with sudden alarm.
